chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Or an equivalent in fasting.' He said: 'The equivalent of the sacrifice is whatever amount it reaches, which he gives in charity. If he does not have it, then he should fast for the equivalent amount; for every meal of a poor person, one day.'
And whenever the value of the ransom exceeds the cost of feeding sixty poor people, he is not bound to do more than that. If it is less than that, that suffices for him.

key_terms.عَدْلُ الْهَدْيِ: Equivalent value of the sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative expiation if one cannot afford to sacrifice an animal for breaking the pilgrimage state?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the proportional mechanism of kaffarah for breaking ihram, establishing that fasting serves as a substitute for feeding when the cost of the sacrificial animal exceeds the capacity to feed sixty poor people. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease and proportionality, ensuring the expiation remains manageable by linking the fasting days directly to the monetary value of the hady relative to the standard feeding rate. It underscores the flexibility in fulfilling religious obligations based on individual financial capability, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh.
